item.title: ‘Sweetheart Deal’: Lawmakers Slam Live Nation’s DOJ Settlement & Urge Ticketmaster Breakup
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends. Today, we're talking about the controversy surrounding Live Nation and the federal government's settlement in their antitrust trial.
[Soft music continues in the background]
Host: On Monday, Democratic lawmakers held a "shadow hearing" to criticize the settlement, which they claim was a "sweetheart deal" for Live Nation. The hearing featured witnesses like California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who shed some light on how the Department of Justice's deal came to be. Bonta said the DOJ suddenly "went quiet" midway through the trial, despite their years-long united front in pursuing the case against Live Nation.
[Short audio clip of Rob Bonta's testimony]
Host: Bonta stated, "They bailed. They left us hanging. We're a team, and they left their teammates. They left us flatfooted for a moment, but we regrouped quickly… We were able to fight for more, and we got more." The states ultimately won the case, holding Live Nation liable for monopolizing the artist, venue, and ticketing sides of the live music industry.
[Soft music continues]
Host: Lawmakers, including Sen. Chuck Schumer and Rep. Jamie Raskin, called the settlement a "trivial and pathetic slap on the wrist" and a "complete sellout." They also raised concerns about Live Nation hiring Trump allies to lobby for the deal. The outcome of the case is still uncertain, with a decision on remedies to be made by Judge Arun Subramanian.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for today. Live Nation's ultimate punishment for alleged antitrust violations remains to be seen, but one thing is clear: this case has sparked a heated debate about the future of the live music industry. We'll be keeping an eye on this story as it unfolds. Thanks for tuning in.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
